observations: Photo 0: Front view of a black DSLR body with 'Canon', 'EOS', '5D', 'Mark II' badges visible; rear body cap is on, no lens attached.
Photo 1: Rear view showing LCD screen (appears dark/off, no power-on test shown), viewfinder, and button layout typical of 5D Mark II.
Photo 2: Bottom plate showing model plate 'Canon DS126201', serial number '3761814763', and standard compliance markings.
No lens, battery, charger, memory card, or original box visible in any photo.
No shot of the LCD displaying a shutter count, menu screen, or image to confirm power-on or functionality.
No close-up of a lens element to verify 'no fungus or scratch' since no lens is pictured at all.

response.reason: The body is clearly identified as a Canon EOS 5D Mark II from the badge and bottom plate, but with no lens, no power-on proof, and no shutter-count evidence, it must be priced at worst case as an unverified, body-only unit comparable to lower-tier DSLR listings.
